_readme: GENERATED by scripts/required-checks-generate.sh from check runs actually observed on the sampled shas. Never hand-edit a context string: GitHub validates neither the name nor the app_id, and a typo deadlocks the branch forever (honest-gates D21). The emit is a MERGE onto this file, not an overwrite: a committed context the sample could not render survives, and one that should have rendered and did not is REFUSED by name before the merge can hide it.

enforced=true means protection IS applied to this branch. From this commit an unreadable or absent protection config is a HARD failure in scripts/required-checks-verify.sh — it is no longer a committed pre-flip state. THE REVERSAL IS TWO COMMANDS, and the first one WRITES A RECORD BEFORE it touches the API: `bash scripts/required-checks-apply.sh --disable --confirm --reason "…" --task <id>`, which execs `scripts/breakglass.sh --open --total`, refuses without both a reason and a task, and appends a row to docs/ops/break-glass-log.md before the DELETE; then `bash scripts/breakglass.sh --close --reason "…" --task <id>` to put the full object back. RUN BOTH FROM A CHECKOUT CUT FROM origin/main AT THAT MOMENT. A stale checkout carries the pre-#8253 apply.sh whose --disable block ends in a bare `gh api -X DELETE`: it removes protection, writes NO record, and a verifier who ran this runbook’s own documented string from a 131-commit-behind checkout took main’s protection down for ~74 seconds leaving ZERO rows in the log (D136).

THE SAMPLING RULE, written down rather than tribal (hgw2-s7). The set below is the INTERSECTION over the sampled heads, so the sample decides what may be required. Sample at least TWO heads that are POST-SHIM and DISPATCHER-SUCCEEDED — `Dispatch (changed-path sets)` must be present and successful on each. A head where that name is ABSENT predates the always-running dispatcher, its job-level `if:` decisions were never made, and no re-run rescues it: re-running a workflow that did not exist at that sha produces nothing. Sample ONE head that EXERCISES the Elixir matrix (`Test (Elixir 1.18.1 / OTP 27.0)` rendered and concluded) and ONE that SKIPS it (the same job publishes the uninterpolated template name `Test (Elixir ${{ matrix.elixir }} / OTP ${{ matrix.otp }})`). Both shapes must still render the aggregators, and that is exactly what makes an aggregator — not a leaf job — the only safe thing to require. WAVE 11 DEVIATION, recorded rather than glossed: at flip time no head in the ten-commit window SKIPPED the Elixir matrix — six of the ten carried ZERO check runs at all — so both sampled heads are matrix-EXERCISED. Shape coverage for the two newly registered names was therefore proven by a different instrument: `bash scripts/registration-sample.sh --since 5ddae0dc2` walks the window and requires at least one qualifying head of NEITHER shape; it found three (e34031104, f69cfb1f6, 2c7493909), on each of which `Console gate` and `Cloud gate` both rendered and concluded success, with zero shim defects. This file was generated from e34031104 and 2c7493909.

THE FLOOR IS A SEPARATE ARTIFACT, and regenerating this file without it is how the required set silently shrinks. `bash scripts/required-checks-floor.sh <candidate>` asserts the candidate is a SUPERSET of `git show origin/main:.github/required-checks.json` on context AND app_id. A bare count floor is not enough: a specimen that swaps `Elixir gate` for an advisory keeps the count at 2 and passes it (honest-gates D64, D74).

EXCLUSIONS ARE WHAT THE SAMPLE SAW, never a complete census. A workflow that never triggered on either sampled head renders no name at all, so it cannot appear below. Disqualification is a property of workflow TOPOLOGY, not of a workflow's identity: a workflow is structurally disqualified FOR AS LONG AS it carries a workflow-level `on: paths:` filter, because such a filter emits NO check run on a PR that misses the paths, and a required context that is ABSENT reports 'expected' forever (D18). CORRECTED IN WAVE 11 — this paragraph used to claim `security.yml` was 'still paths-filtered to api/**'. It is not, and has not been since wave 10: security.yml:37 forbids the key from ever returning ('THIS WORKFLOW MUST NEVER REGAIN A WORKFLOW-LEVEL `on: … paths:` KEY') and the file renders a check run on every head. `Security gate` is held out today, and not on topology. CORRECTED IN REVIEW 2026-07-31 — this paragraph used to say the ground was 'it is RED on main', with the bump that clears it open as PR #8222. That was true when the file was generated and stopped being true DURING the wave: 95ace3150 landed the req bump from outside this epic, `Security gate` is green on main head 6e53d2782, and re-running the generator on the post-bump window PROMOTES the name into required protection. The hold therefore moved from the mechanical S5 stage into the generator's hand-maintained S7 list, and the ground is now forward-looking: `Security gate` does not aggregate Sobelow and structurally cannot — needs = [changes, gate-shape, sobelow-inline-overlap, sobelow-baseline-fingerprint, mix-audit], because aggregating a continue-on-error job would LAUNDER a red — so its sole blocking upstream is mix-audit, which runs mix_audit against a LIVE advisory database. A CVE published tomorrow reds it on every open PR with no change to this repo: a permanently correct red that no PR can clear, which is exactly what branch protection must never pin. Requiring it needs its own wave — a documented policy for who clears a fleet-wide advisory red, plus a fresh deadlock sweep — not a silent promotion by the next regeneration. Its leaves are excluded WITH it (S6): promoting the leaves of a disqualified aggregator re-implements that aggregator at leaf granularity, forever. `console-harness.yml` and `cloud.yml` were excluded on genuine topology grounds, were shimmed in wave 9, have rendered on real heads since, and are registered by THIS file. Two legacy Vercel commit statuses fail on EVERY sha repo-wide and live in a different namespace (R0/R3); they can never be required.

Every protection field is enumerated INCLUDING the falses: the PUT does not converge omitted state (allow_force_pushes resets, required_linear_history and required_conversation_resolution do NOT). See honest-gates D41.

No workflow carries a merge_group trigger and this repo is user-owned (no merge queue), so queue semantics are not a variable today. If the repo ever moves to an org and the merge queue is enabled, every required check would sit Pending-forever in the merge group on day one.

OPERATIONAL: a required context whose LATEST run on the head concluded `cancelled` blocks the merge with a third refusal shape (`... is cancelled.`, honest-gates D38) and clears only on a re-run or a push. THIS DOES NOT APPLY TO THE FOUR AGGREGATORS (hgw4-bl-elixir-gate-cancelled-arm): they are `if: always()` jobs that DECIDE over `needs.<job>.result`, so a cancelled UPSTREAM makes the aggregator conclude `failure`, never `cancelled` — MEASURED on sha 6539d929, where five upstream jobs read completed|cancelled while `Elixir gate` read completed|failure and the merge refused with `is failing.`, not `is cancelled.` As of the cancelled-arm split in elixir.yml's decide(), that red now NAMES cancellation in the step log and the `::error::` and prescribes a new head sha. The `is cancelled.` shape is still reachable for a NON-aggregator required context — one whose own job is cancelled outright — so the merge protocol must still expect it.

MERGE PROTOCOL: `scripts/bp-merge.sh`, argument-free, from the PR branch's own worktree. The admin bypass is refused server-side under enforce_admins:true and is no longer this repo's protocol. `allow_auto_merge` stays FALSE on purpose: this fleet stacks branches, and a PR whose checks go green forty minutes later would land into a main that has moved, in an order nobody chose. bp-merge polls and merges in the FOREGROUND.

S4 PATHS-FILTERED: go-format.yml carries a workflow-level `on: pull_request: paths:` filter (**.go, the workflow itself, scripts/go-format-drift-ceiling.sh, .go-format-drift-ceiling), so on a PR that touches none of them this name is ABSENT — and a required absent context reports 'expected' forever (D18). ADDED BY HAND 2026-08-08 (wave 56 S4), and the MECHANISM is the point, not the row: this name renders `(blocking)` in its own title and had never appeared anywhere in this repo's merge-authority census — `grep -c gofmt` was 0 in this file (checks AND exclusions) and 0 in docs/ops/merge-gates.md. It is not a dud; it runs and passes ('OK: 739 Go files scanned; 0 off-roster drift; roster holds 0 grandfathered file(s)'). It was invisible BY CONSTRUCTION: this file's own `_readme` concedes 'EXCLUSIONS ARE WHAT THE SAMPLE SAW, never a complete census' — the generator can only write down names that RENDERED on the sampled heads, so every paths-filtered workflow that missed those heads is unseeable, and go-format.yml is the specimen that proves the blind spot rather than an oversight anyone could have caught by re-reading. The same mechanism is lossy in the other direction and nothing reports it: four names previously enumerated here (PR task gate self-test, Re-land advisory, Filebase aesthetics gate, Boundary gate) have SILENTLY LEFT this list on regeneration. So do not read the absence of a name from this array as evidence that no such gate exists — read it as 'the sample did not see it'. THIS ROW NOW SURVIVES A REGENERATION, and it did not until 2026-08-09 (wave 57). The history is the point, because it is the same disease twice: the sentence that first stood here ('hand-added rows like this one survive regeneration, the emit is a MERGE not an overwrite') was false, and its correction ('re-add this row by hand after any regeneration') was a guard that cannot lose because it is not a guard — a human remembering is not a mechanism. WHAT WAS TRUE THEN: the MERGE the `_readme` promises covered `_readme` and `.protection.required_status_checks.checks` (a base-first union, `(($b.protection...checks) // []) + $checks | unique_by(.context)`), while `.exclusions` was emitted as `exclusions: $exclusions` from the array THIS run derived, never reading `$b.exclusions` — so over the frozen fixture pair in scripts/fixtures/registration-flip the generator took 25 exclusion rows IN and wrote 18 OUT, exit 0, zero bytes on stderr, and a paths-filtered name can never re-enter the derived set because stage 2 iterates only names that RENDERED on the sampled heads. WHAT IS TRUE NOW: `.exclusions` is emitted as the SAME base-first union, with the DERIVED reason winning where both sides carry a row, so the merge CARRIES this one; and a run that cannot re-derive a committed exclusion REFUSES BY NAME until it is acknowledged one name at a time with `--expect-unrendered`, so the carry can never be silent. Both arms are mutation-proven in scripts/required-checks.test.sh section 14b. A census guard that reds on any blocking-shaped job name outside required ∪ exclusions ∪ transitive-needs is filed separately as cchi-w57-blocking-shaped-name-census-guard — and THAT task, not this sentence, is where the count of such names belongs: a figure typed here has no producer and goes stale in its own commit, which is exactly what happened to the bare '35 such names exist today' that stood here, falsified by the very commit that wrote it (085cc8719).

(1) 'green on main' was FALSE — on main head 070c7584b `bash scripts/required-checks.test.sh --hermetic` ended '115 passed, 1 failed', its §18 protection-claim census reddening on the wave-35 write-up OF ITSELF. That specific failure is fixed by the quoted-pattern fence in the same commit as this correction, but the greenness claim is DROPPED rather than re-asserted: a spec file cannot know a check's colour, only the run can, and a stale colour written here is exactly the kind of claim this epic exists to delete. (2) 'Re-evaluate once #8222 lands or is rebased' was a trigger that can NEVER FIRE — #8222 is CLOSED with mergedAt null (`gh pr view 8222 --json state,mergedAt`), so the exclusion sealed itself shut and would have outlived every reason it names. THE HOLD ITSELF STANDS, on ground that is live and re-measurable: required-checks-drift.yml is deliberately path-UNFILTERED, so every open PR renders this name from its own head; today those verdicts are stale (rendered 07-31..08-05, before the ledger merge) and three of the seven open PRs are CONFLICTING and do not render the name at all — registering it today deadlocks 7 of 7 under enforce_admins. THE REPLACEMENT TRIGGER, checkable by anyone and owned by nobody's memory: the spec gate is green on main HEAD, and a fresh `scripts/registration-deadlock-sweep.sh` run for this context reports zero casualties. Tracked as cch-w37-bl-register-spec-gate-human-gate.

S7 EXCLUDED BY DECISION: the dispatcher job of compose-smoke.yml, held out on purpose — and NOT on either mechanical leaf class, which was CHECKED rather than assumed from the name. NOT S3: that class reads `an upstream `needs` of a REQUIRED aggregator`, and this job's aggregator is `Compose smoke` (job `compose-gate`), which does not appear in this file's required checks — registering it is a separate HUMAN GATE, task shb-bl-register-compose-smoke, which the workflow that created the name deliberately did not take. NOT S6 either: that class reads `an upstream `needs` of an aggregator this run EXCLUDED`, and `Compose smoke` is absent from this array too. So the four Dispatch siblings are NOT precedent for a mechanical class here, and reading them as one is the trap this row exists to close: `Dispatch (cloud paths)`, `Dispatch (console paths)` and `Dispatch (changed-path sets)` are S3 because `Cloud gate`, `Console gate` and `Elixir gate` ARE required, and `Dispatch (security paths)` is S6 because `Security gate` IS excluded. This one is the third case — a leaf of an aggregator that is neither — which is precisely why no stage ever emitted a row for it, and why its absence is a gap in the LEDGER rather than a gap in the derivation. THE GROUND FOR THE HOLD is the one S3 and S6 both encode, applied to an aggregator nobody has yet decided to require: promoting a leaf re-implements its gate at leaf granularity and pins the gate's internals as a contract. THE SECOND GROUND IS WHAT A GREEN HERE WOULD MEAN, and it is the stronger one: `compose-smoke.yml`'s dispatcher only computes a changed-path verdict — `refusal-arm` and `green-arm` can both be skipped, and the aggregator can be RED, while this job reports success. Requiring it would pin a name whose green certifies nothing about the compose stack, on every PR, forever. THE REPLACEMENT TRIGGER, owned by a run and not by anyone's memory: once `Compose smoke` is itself registered under shb-bl-register-compose-smoke, the next regeneration derives this name as S3 and the DERIVED reason wins over this text. ADDED BY HAND 2026-09-01 (cgsiw-bl-compose-smoke-dispatch-no-ledger-row): both `generated_from_shas` predate compose-smoke.yml, which did not exist until 2026-08-09, so no stage in this generator can re-derive this row today — the next run REFUSES BY NAME until it is acknowledged with `--expect-unrendered 'Dispatch (compose-smoke paths)'`, exactly the carry the gofmt row above documents.

S7 EXCLUDED BY DECISION, and it must NEVER be promoted: pr-task-gate.yml job `pr-task-gate-selftest` is the hermetic harness for `PR references an active task` — the only required context any guard script in this repo publishes — and the workflow's own comment records why the harness is deliberately NOT a `needs:` of that gate: GitHub counts a `skipped` conclusion as SATISFYING a required context (D19), so wiring the harness upstream would let a RED harness turn the gate itself into a green required check. Requiring the harness NAME does not answer that hazard either; it only adds a second red-capable name to branch protection with no authority over what the gate decides. So the safe direction is to CLASSIFY the name here, never to promote it. WHY IT WAS UNCLASSIFIED RATHER THAN OVERLOOKED, and this is a defect in the generator's census, not in anyone's reading: pr-task-gate.yml is `on: pull_request:` with no push arm, while both `generated_from_shas` are main PUSH heads — so neither this name NOR `PR references an active task` renders on the sampled window, and the census is structurally blind to EVERY pull_request-only check name. The required context itself survives only via this file's MERGE-not-overwrite rule. THIS ROW DOES NOT CLOSE THAT GAP and must not be read as closing it: an S8 PULL-REQUEST-ONLY stage, or sampling a PR head instead of only push shas, is tracked as cgsi-bl-pr-task-gate-selftest-unclassified, whose SECOND criterion stays open. This row answers only its first — that the name carries an explicit ledger entry naming why it is not required. It also restores one of the four names the gofmt row above records as having SILENTLY LEFT this array on a regeneration; the other three (Re-land advisory, Filebase aesthetics gate, Boundary gate) are still unledgered and are NOT claimed by this row. ADDED BY HAND 2026-09-01 (cgsiw-bl-compose-smoke-dispatch-no-ledger-row): no stage can re-derive it from push heads, so the next run REFUSES BY NAME until it is acknowledged with `--expect-unrendered 'PR task gate self-test'`.
